headline:

body:

kicker: CANCHA NOTES / ON & OFF THE PITCH
headline:
Tryout or training?
Know the difference.
body: Choose the session for the step you actually want.
cta: Save this before you sign up.
questions: A training session
Practice and coaching. It may have no link to team selection.
An evaluation
A coach assesses fit. Attendance does not guarantee a roster place.
A camp or showcase
Ask who runs it, who it serves and which coaches are confirmed.
A team registration
Check the season, total cost and whether a place is confirmed.
caption:
A training session, an evaluation and a team place are three different things.

Before paying or travelling, ask what the session actually includes and what happens afterward. If you want a team, ask about current recruitment. If you want practice, check the age and skill group.

Build a shortlist on Cancha, then confirm the details directly.

kicker: CANCHA NOTES / ON & OFF THE PITCH
headline:
Your next role
could be on the sideline.
body: You don’t need to guess where to start.
cta: Send this to someone who wants to coach.
questions: Pick the environment
Youth club, school, recreational league or a specialist role.
Read the actual role
Hours, responsibilities, required experience and compensation.
Check the pathway
Use FYSA and U.S. Soccer for official coaching-course guidance.
Ask about support
Who mentors coaches, plans sessions and handles club policies?
caption:
Love explaining the game? Coaching is one route into soccer beyond playing.

Start with an actual club role and its requirements. Then use the official FYSA/U.S. Soccer pathway to understand which course is appropriate; completing a course alone does not promise a job.

kicker: CANCHA NOTES / ON & OFF THE PITCH
headline:
Watch one match.
Notice more.
body: A small first project for a future soccer analyst.
questions: Pick one question
For example: how does a team move the ball out of its own half?
Choose a few tags
Build-up shape, pressure, progression and the outcome.
Record clear examples
Use footage you have permission to analyse and share.
Write one finding
Explain what the clips show, and what they cannot prove.
caption:
You can start learning analysis with one clear question, rather than a dashboard full of numbers.

Use footage you can lawfully work with, define a few consistent tags and explain the examples. Avoid drawing a season-long conclusion from one match.

We’ve collected official video/data-analysis courses alongside coaching and player-development resources:
https://pioneering-friday-005497.framer.app/training
